nA.text:
THE JOURNEY, EVERYWHERE

The stage track and “how it got here” were the same object seen twice — one facing forward, one back. Drawn once, down the side, the history stops being a section: each stage carries what happened inside it.

The supplier chip then sits AT the stage where it is true, instead of floating above everything.

The ··· and the phone follow the same design. The phone keeps a horizontal track: 210px of spine is half of a 390px screen.

n3.text:
The decision is which of two numbers to bill, and today both are inside a sentence: “Billing what was picked makes this order 2,243,000 UGX, down from 2,321,000 UGX.”

So show the two numbers and let one be picked. The button then says what it will do — “Bill 1 Roll” — instead of “Supplied in full anyway” sitting beside “Bill for what was picked”, which are the same shape and opposite meanings.

n4.text:
A buying round is a set of PLACES somebody drives to, so the object on the screen should be the place.

One card per stop, holding everything that stop needs: what it costs to carry, what is on it, whether anybody has been sent, and the one act.

That removes three things at once — the supplier repeated on every row, the amber band about lines nobody is buying, and the footer sentence about what this dialog does not do. Each card says its own state instead.

n5.text:
A delivery round is the same object as a buying round, pointed the other way: a set of PLACES, with orders on each and somebody carrying them. So it gets the same card, and the two screens become one thing to learn.

Gone with the table: the destination repeated on every row under a head that already names it, four identical “Delivered” buttons, and twenty-two words of footer saying what marking delivered does and that an empty run closes itself — both true every time, news never.

The run with no place on file is not a run yet, so it wears an amber mark and its act is to fix that.

nE.text:
WHAT IT REPLACES

900 × 596 for a one-line order, and about 150 words. The journey is 680 × 420.

Gone: the sentence about who has it, “not yet” four times, the WHAT TO TELL THE CLIENT band, the always-open history, two empty photo frames, the paragraph explaining what cost means, “nothing is owed until it is delivered”, and “nothing here sends itself”.
